source_loc.method: Physical lines including comments, blanks and docstrings, measured with find/wc at the pinned commits. Whole-repository and layer-increment scopes are reported separately and are not code-efficiency ratios.

equivalent_qualification_axes.assessment: Both cover the requested axes with deterministic local evidence and explicit live blockers. Counts are disclosed rather than padded; framework case-count, event-count and risk-count parity are not claimed.

framework_acceleration: Temporal supplies durable task scheduling, retries, timers, signals, cancellation delivery, workflow replay and worker recovery mechanics.
LangGraph supplies bounded fanout/fanin, reducers and checkpoint mechanics.
FastAPI, Pydantic, OpenTelemetry, MCP/A2A SDKs and React/TanStack supply protocol, validation, delivery, telemetry and UI mechanics.
The Layer 15 runner composes the existing 58 cross-layer cases instead of adding a second qualification product implementation.
framework_complexity: Temporal Cloud adds namespace, payload codec, authentication, retention, versioning, capacity, cost and failover qualification.
LangGraph adds checkpoint compatibility, migration and pruning operations while remaining non-authoritative.
Framework and application retry/state ownership must be separated to avoid duplicate work or authority leakage.
The framework dependency closure is larger than the custom pinned closure.
remaining_custom_controls: identity, tenant, current purpose/RBAC and forced RLS
application events, dual hashes, idempotency, inbox/outbox and projections
budget reservation, provider/connector quotas and reconciliation
evidence provenance, citations, critic policy and deterministic aggregation
approval, fencing, receipts, verification, compensation and ambiguity
sandbox policy, artifact trust, cleanup and isolation readiness
memory acceptance, retention, legal hold, erasure and context policy
MCP/A2A trust, workload identity, proposal-only effects and revocation
telemetry redaction, readiness, release, compliance and go-live evidence

performance_methodology.framework: Fixed serial synthetic inputs with local p50/p95/p99, throughput and error budgets; four service/browser/restore profiles remain environment-gated.
performance_methodology.custom: Pinned report used three samples and one warmup on an unnormalized shared developer host.
performance_methodology.comparison: Neither report supports production extrapolation or cross-repository latency ranking.

lock_in: Temporal history, namespace and Worker Deployment APIs
LangGraph checkpoint serialization and graph-version compatibility
official SDK upgrade and transitive dependency surfaces
escape: ledger-grounded projection rebuild independent of framework state
opaque Temporal messages and disposable LangGraph checkpoints
migration rehearsal requiring identical application projections

parity_gaps: Framework has 58 governed cases versus custom 127 and does not claim catalog-count parity.
Framework canonical output does not manufacture custom's 203-event/nine-stream shape because event schemas and layer implementations differ.
Framework PostgreSQL/pgvector, Temporal, browser and logical restore profiles remain separate environment gates.
Neither side supplies live production capacity, chaos, identity, managed recovery, independent review or certification evidence.
A production framework export/replacement rehearsal with identical projections remains required.
